correctness.rationale: Intrinsic wide Euclidean cone has unique geodesics, and the apex route is minimizing precisely when shorter circular angular separation is at least π; for k cyclic ordered azimuths this means all k gaps at least π. A fixed labeled anchor makes the k-1 free gaps uniformly distributed on simplex of total θ; translation by (π,...,π) gives exact success probability (δ/θ)^(k-1) and conditional Dirichlet(1,...,1), δ=θ-kπ>0, with zero for δ<=0. Summing over k-subsets gives expectation. In critical δ=c n^-k/(k-1), dissociated indicators have p=O(n^-k), b1=O(n^-1). For two cliques sharing s labels all their distinct nonanchor vertices lie in k-1 disjoint near-jπ intervals total length ≤(k-1)δ, giving b2 bounded by sum_s n^(2k-s) δ^(2k-s-1)=O(n^-1/(k-1)); Chen–Stein yields TV rate and Poisson mean. The variance method proves the supercritical zero-one direction. The exact shared-pair overlap for k=3 integrates two triangular width functions yielding q=2δ^3/(3θ^3); shared-one-vertex indicators are independent conditional on common anchor. Inspected supplied checker actual conditions, labeled anchor and finite Monte Carlo; finite tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Natural higher-order obstruction to apex-avoiding minimizers on a wide metric cone: determines exact first appearance of all-k pairwise apex-passing structures and a sharp Poisson window, plus conditional shape law.
